sections.heading: C — License eligibility and identity
sections.markdown:
## C — License eligibility and identity (part one)

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
Anyone who lives in West Virginia and wants to drive a motor vehicle on public roads must hold a West Virginia driver's license unless expressly exempt, and must carry that license while driving [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
A person operating a motor vehicle in the armed services of the United States while performing official duties is exempt from the West Virginia license requirement [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
A nonresident who is at least sixteen years old and holds a valid license from another state or country is exempt from needing a West Virginia license, but only for ninety days in a calendar year [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
A nonresident attending a West Virginia college or university who holds a valid license from another state is exempt from the West Virginia license requirement [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
A habitual user of alcoholic beverages or a person addicted to narcotic drugs can be denied a driver's license [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
A person whose driver's license has been suspended or revoked by West Virginia, another state or a foreign jurisdiction can be denied a license until that suspension or revocation period expires [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
A license can be denied to anyone the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles has good cause to believe would endanger public safety or welfare when operating a motor vehicle [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
A person under the age of eighteen who is neither enrolled in nor graduated from an approved educational institution can be denied a driver's license [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
In twenty eleven West Virginia adopted the federal licensing standards of the REAL ID Act of two thousand five, a secure license and identification card program meant to improve the integrity and security of all driver's licenses and ID cards nationwide [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A01
Every first-time license applicant must bring documents proving identity, Social Security number, any legal name change that has ever occurred, and West Virginia residency, and the DMV scans the documents securely and returns them [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A01
A license or ID card certified as REAL ID compliant carries a gold star on its face showing that it meets full federal requirements for use at airports and other designated federal facilities across the country [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A01
A license applied for at any DMV location arrives at the applicant's address by mail in approximately fifteen to twenty business days, and a temporary license issued when the application is accepted covers the production and shipping time [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
West Virginia offers two kinds of driver's license and ID card, a Not For Federal Use card and a REAL ID or For Federal Use card with a gold star, and the documents you must bring depend on which type you choose [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
A renewal applicant for a Not For Federal Use card with no changes brings only the current license or ID card and the renewal application, while an address change requires two proofs of West Virginia residency and a legal name change requires proof of that change [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
If a driver's license is lost, stolen or destroyed, a duplicate can be requested online or at a Regional Office, with proof of any legal name change and two residency proofs if the address changed since the last card [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A02
New, transfer and expired-license applicants must provide one proof of identity, their Social Security number, two proofs of West Virginia residency showing name and physical address, and proof of legal name change if the name differs from the identity document [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A02
The handbook treats as a first-time applicant anyone who has never held a driver's license or ID card, who is transferring an out-of-state license, or whose West Virginia license has been expired for more than three years [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A02
An applicant transferring a license from another state must also hand in the current out-of-state license or present a certified driving record from that state dated thirty days or less before the application [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A02
A For Federal Use renewal or duplicate applicant must provide one proof of identity, a Social Security number, two proofs of West Virginia residency with name and physical address, and proof of legal name change if the name has ever changed [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A02
The For Federal Use card costs an additional ten dollars and is mailed to the applicant in fifteen to twenty business days, with a temporary license issued when the application is accepted [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A03
An original or certified copy of a United States birth certificate proves identity, including State Department and military birth certificates, but hospital birth certificates and Bureau of Census records are not acceptable [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A03
A valid United States passport or passport card is an acceptable proof of identity [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A03
A foreign-born applicant may prove identity with a valid, unexpired Department of Homeland Security document such as a Permanent Resident Card, an employment authorization document, a certificate of naturalization or citizenship, a consular report of birth abroad, or a foreign passport carrying a valid United States visa with the approved arrival record of the most recent admittance [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A03
You must present exactly one proof of identity and must provide your Social Security number, and your full legal name must match the name on file with the Social Security Administration because the DMV checks every number with that agency [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A03
If your name or date of birth does not match Social Security Administration records, the problem must be corrected before an instruction permit, license or identification card can be issued [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A03
An applicant who is not eligible for a Social Security number must submit a letter from the Social Security Administration stating that ineligibility [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A03
Acceptable proof of Social Security number is the original card in your current legal name, an original Wage and Tax Statement or a payroll stub showing the employer's name and identification number along with your name, address and number, or a ten ninety-nine form showing your full number and name, and a photocopy of the Wage and Tax Statement is not acceptable [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

sections.heading: C — License eligibility and identity
sections.markdown:
## C — License eligibility and identity (part two)

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A04
Proof of legal name change is required if your name has ever changed, because the DMV must be able to link every legal name you have used [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A04
Acceptable proof of a legal name change is a marriage certificate for each marriage if married more than once, an amended birth certificate, a court order or a divorce decree showing the legal name, while souvenir marriage documents and minister's copies are not acceptable [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A04
Two proofs of West Virginia residency are required, documents showing a post office box are not acceptable, any recurring document such as a utility bill cannot be more than ninety days old, and a married applicant may use documents in the spouse's name together with a marriage certificate [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A04
Residency proofs include a West Virginia utility bill that is not a termination notice, tax records with a West Virginia street address, mortgage or homeowner insurance documents, a voter registration card, a vehicle registration card, a bank statement, a rental or lease agreement, an auto insurance card, a hunting license and a paycheck stub from a West Virginia employer showing a current physical address that is not handwritten [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A04
Further residency proofs include a college admissions letter showing in-state residency, a nine one one address letter, a Social Security benefits letter, a Post Office letter assigning a new physical West Virginia address, a Wage and Tax Statement not more than eighteen months old, and a letter from a shelter, hotel, nursing home or similar facility giving its physical address and stating that the applicant lives there [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A05
An applicant for any driver's license or identification card must be a West Virginia resident, and the DMV will not license or issue a card to anyone who does not give a West Virginia physical address [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A05
A former West Virginia resident who now lives elsewhere may not renew a West Virginia license or identification card until residency in the state is established again [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A05
Once a new resident's two residency documents have been scanned into the record, later renewals or transactions require two residency documents again only if the physical address has changed [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A05
Every license applicant and every renewing driver is reviewed through the Problem Driver Point System, a national driver registry that tracks violations and suspensions from state to state [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A05
The DMV is prohibited from licensing a driver whose record shows an unsettled problem in another state or jurisdiction, so pending citations and suspensions elsewhere must be satisfied before applying for or renewing a West Virginia license [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A05
When another state reports an unpaid citation, the West Virginia DMV notifies the driver by certified mail at the address in its system, allows a certain amount of time to resolve it, and then suspends the license, and the driver must supply proof of payment or of satisfying the court order before reinstatement [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F39 | anchor: A05
Unpaid citations remain the driver's own responsibility, and the court should not be expected to notify the DMV when an unpaid citation is resolved [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F40 | anchor: A06
A first-time applicant for an instruction permit, driver's license or identification card must provide a Social Security number, one proof of identity, two proofs of West Virginia residency and the application form the DMV provides, plus name-change documents such as a certified marriage certificate, divorce decree or court order when the name has changed [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F41 | anchor: A06
A new resident with a valid, unexpired out-of-state license may transfer it after passing a vision screening, completing a brief alcohol awareness course and surrendering the out-of-state license, and must present every document required of a first-time applicant [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F42 | anchor: A06
New residents who want to drive in West Virginia must apply for a West Virginia license within thirty days of establishing residency, and a motorcycle endorsement on the old license transfers for an additional fee [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F43 | anchor: A06
If the out-of-state license has been expired for more than three years, the new resident must take every examination required of a first-time applicant, and a new resident who cannot produce the out-of-state license must obtain a certified driving record from the former state to waive testing [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F44 | anchor: A06
A new resident whose out-of-state license is suspended or revoked will not be licensed in West Virginia until the Problem Driver Point System issues a clearance, and driving in the state on a license suspended or revoked anywhere is illegal [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F45 | anchor: A06
A driver who changes address must notify the DMV in writing within twenty days, failure to do so can bring a fine or imprisonment, and telling only the Post Office does not update the DMV record or forward DMV mail [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F46 | anchor: A07
To obtain a duplicate license you present two residency documents if your address changed and evidence of any name change, you must supply your Social Security number if it is missing or wrong in the DMV database, and a non-citizen must present the documents that verify legal status, identity and residency [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F47 | anchor: A07
Anyone renewing a West Virginia license, including a commercial driver's license, that has been expired for three years or more must retest through the full examination process with all first-time documents, and an expired out-of-state license also requires retesting [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F48 | anchor: A07
Applicants aged fifteen to seventeen receive a vertical license or instruction permit color-coded red, applicants aged eighteen to twenty receive a vertical card color-coded blue, and applicants twenty-one or older receive a horizontal license with a landscape background [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F49 | anchor: A08
An immigrant applying for a permit, license or identification card provides a Social Security number, two proofs of West Virginia residency, and one of a Permanent Resident Card, a valid temporary resident stamp in a foreign passport with English translation or on the arrival record, or a valid re-entry permit [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F50 | anchor: A08
A non-immigrant applicant provides a Social Security number or a Social Security Administration denial letter, two residency proofs, a valid foreign passport, the federal arrival record, a visa when the applicant's nation requires one, original documents verifying status and authorized stay, and written school verification for student statuses or employer verification for work statuses [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F51 | anchor: A08
A refugee applicant provides a Social Security number or denial letter, two residency proofs, an arrival record showing the grant of refugee status, a Reception and Placement Program Assurance form, and written verification of identity and residency from an employee of a State Department approved sponsoring organization [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F52 | anchor: A08
A refugee without an approved sponsoring organization, or a person seeking asylum, provides two residency proofs, a Social Security number or denial letter, an arrival record stamped as refugee or asylee, and employment authorization documents [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

ranked.label: Who must be licensed, exemptions and denials
Core document set for first-time applicants
Identity, Social Security and name-change proofs
New residents, transfers and expired licenses
Card types, mailing and color coding

items.why: Who must be licensed, who is exempt and which documents to bring are recall items served by standard flashcards and quiz questions, so no separate practice mode is needed.

corpus_stability.reason: The West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook is a periodically revised official edition, so its licensing-requirements chapter changes at most with a new edition.
